title: I-power torsion modules are unchanged by a flat base change that is an isomorphism modulo I
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a flat ring map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal such that the ring map $R/I\to S/IS$ induced by $\varphi$ is an isomorphism ($IS$ the ideal of $S$ generated by $\varphi(I)$). An $R$-module $T$ is *$I$-power torsion* if for every $x\in T$ there is $n\ge1$ with $I^nx=0$. Then for every $I$-power torsion $R$-module $T$ the $R$-linear map $T\to T\otimes_RS$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, to the base change of $T$ [def-weil-module-base-change] is bijective.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05E9 (lemma-neighbourhood-isomorphism, line 24264), implication (2) => (1); its standing hypothesis, the equivalent conditions of Lemma 05E7 (lemma-characterize-flatness-on-torsion), holds because an isomorphism R/I -> S/IS is faithfully flat (as used at the start of the proof of Lemma 05EC)

proof.text: Equip S with the R-algebra structure φ.toAlgebra and install Module.Flat R S from hflat. Quotient ring extensionality identifies the induced quotientMap with the given ring equivalence, yielding bijectivity modulo I. Apply RingHom.bijective_quotientMap_pow_of_flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-iso-mod-ideal-powers] to obtain bijectivity modulo I^n for all n ≥ 1.

Prove the killed-module case in the private helper killedModule_baseChange_bijective. For an ideal J annihilating M, form the R-linear q:S → R/J from the inverse quotient algebra equivalence. J times M is zero. The tensor quotient equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring], followed by the quotient-by-zero equivalence, composes with 1 tensor q to give d:M tensor S → M with d(x tensor 1)=x; hence the comparison is injective. For surjectivity, ideal-span induction shows x tensor bs=0 for b in JS: for a generator φ(r), balance the tensor and use rx=0; addition and multiplication preserve vanishing. Surjectivity modulo J gives r with s-φ(r) in JS, so x tensor s=(rx) tensor 1. Tensor induction then represents zero, each pure tensor, and each sum as y tensor 1. All these steps are fully proved in Lean; flatness is not required in this helper.

For x in T choose n ≥ 1 annihilating x. Let N=Submodule.torsionBySet R T (I^n), the constructed submodule of elements killed by I^n. Then x lies in N and every element of I^n annihilates N. Apply the helper of step 2 with J=I^n and step 1 to obtain bijectivity of N → N tensor S. No object is chosen from an unproved existence theorem.

Prove injectivity by the zero kernel criterion. If x tensor 1=0, choose N from step 3. Flatness preserves injectivity of N.subtype after tensoring [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], so the tensor of x viewed in N with 1 is zero. The injective comparison for N forces x=0. For surjectivity induct on the ambient tensor: zero lifts to zero; for x tensor s choose N containing x, lift the corresponding pure tensor in N tensor S using its surjective comparison, and map the equality through N.subtype.rTensor S; lifts of two summands add. This replaces the categorical colimit passage with an explicit elementwise argument and tensor induction.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 05E9 (2) => (1), killed-module case and bounded torsion submodules; use the proved flat-iso-mod-ideal-powers lemma in place of module induction and tensor induction in place of categorical colimits.

Not a Mathlib leaf (LeanSearch, LeanFinder, Loogle, grep; nothing on I-power torsion modules under base change). Proof follows 05E9 (2)=>(1) in four steps: set-up and naturality of x -> x(x)1; the case IM = 0 with the identification M(x)_R S = M (written as an explicit inverse r(x(x)s) = psi^{-1}(s mod IS)x); induction P(n) => P(n+1) with 0 -> I^nM -> M -> M/I^nM -> 0, flatness, right exactness and the short five lemma; the general case as the colimit of the T_n = T[I^n] with tensor products commuting with colimits, the inverse built from the two colimit properties. Only flatness and R/I = S/IS are used; the faithful flatness of the 05E7 standing hypothesis is not needed. Statement kept; both citers (formal-glueing-isogeny step 5, formal-glueing-complex-exact step 6) use only bijectivity of x -> x(x)1, which is what the statement gives.
